audit_findings.title: Acquisition-funded growth may be projected as if it were free organic growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $666.8 million of acquisition cash paid during 2023-2025 ($313.4m + $96.3m + $257.1m); future sustaining acquisition spend unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical acquired earnings enter the OE trend and projected growth, while acquisition consideration is absent from projected reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: We have completed 17 acquisitions since 2016, and eight acquisitions in the last three years, all of which were strategic and complementary acquisitions that expanded our addressable market and that we believe will enable value creation through greater scale and growth opportunities.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates substantial acquisition spending and that acquired businesses contributed to reported growth. It does not establish that the 8%-10% forecast requires continued acquisitions, especially given H1 2026 organic sales growth of 12.1%. Nevertheless, acquisition spending is large relative to $335.1 million of anchor OE, so treating acquisition-dependent growth as costless could materially overstate operating value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild historical OE on a constant organic perimeter, reconcile organic and acquired OE growth, and rerun the scenarios using either organic growth or an explicit recurring acquisition-investment deduction.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor and current equity claim use different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $71.4 million of acquired sales and $3.8 million of acquired segment earnings in H1 2026; pro forma owner earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A partial-year FY2025 OE anchor is grown as though it represents the businesses owned at the June 2026 bridge date.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended 2025, the Company completed the acquisitions of Superior, Haws, EasyWater and I-CON, resulting in an increase in goodwill within the Americas segment of $ 111.6 million, and completed the acquisition of Saudi Cast resulting in an increase in goodwill within the APMEA segment of $ 17.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: several acquisitions contributed only weeks to FY2025 but are fully owned at the bridge date. This may understate normalized starting OE, while the forecast could overstate growth by treating the acquired earnings ramp as organic growth. The filings do not provide pro forma owner earnings, so the net value effect and materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare full-year pro forma OE for every business owned on June 28, 2026, including taxes, working capital, maintenance investment and financing costs, then rerun all scenarios from that common perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not all be distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $220.2 million of foreign cash equals $6.51/share and 3.4% of base equity value; even removing all $347.9 million reduces value by only $10.28/share, or 5.3%
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash after purging interest income, without deducting repatriation leakage or required operating liquidity.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to recording the Toll Tax as part of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, our intent, other than with respect to the one-time repatriation of foreign earnings in 2023, has been to permanently reinvest undistributed earnings of foreign subsidiaries, and we do not have any current plans to repatriate additional post-Toll Tax foreign earnings to fund operations in the United States.
audit_findings.explanation: Free distributability is not demonstrated: 63.3% of cash is held abroad and management intends to reinvest foreign earnings. However, even the extreme removal of every dollar of cash would reduce base value from $193.47 to about $183.19 per share, still far below the $363.13 market price. The issue therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion, although the bridge should label cash availability more carefully.
audit_findings.action: Determine domestic excess cash, foreign cash net of withholding and state taxes, and minimum operating liquidity; update the bridge classification without changing operating OE.

audit_findings.title: Multi-year ERP implementation cash costs may escape the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $25-$30 million planned for 2026, equal to 7.5%-9.0% of $335.1 million anchor OE; gross capitalized implementation costs increased $12.8 million in 2025 while amortization was $1.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized cloud-implementation cash may avoid the property-capex deduction and enter earnings only through delayed amortization, overstating OE during deployment.
audit_findings.evidence: We also anticipate investing approximately $25 million to $30 million during 2026 related to our multi-year cloud-based SAP ERP system implementation for our Americas and APMEA regions.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting lag is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation separately deducted capitalized cloud-computing payments. If it did not, projected distributable cash is overstated. The disclosed 2026 amount is meaningful relative to annual OE, but the remaining rollout duration and recurring amount are not established, preventing a reliable valuation impact calculation.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized ERP cash payments from the cash-flow accounts into each historical OE calculation, obtain the annual rollout schedule, and rerun OE with all implementation cash deducted in the years paid.

audit_findings.title: An unquantified environmental claim may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured Chemetco remediation payment would reduce future OE or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is unable to estimate a range of reasonably possible loss for the above matter in which damages have not been specified because: (i) the FS process for the first portion of the Site has not been completed, and the RI/FS process for the remainder of the Site has not yet been initiated, to determine what remediation plans will be implemented and the costs of such plans; (ii) the total amount of material sent to the Site, and the total number of PRPs who may or may not agree to fund or perform any remediation, have not been determined; (iii) the share contribution for PRPs to any remediation has not been determined; and (iv) the number of years required to implement a remediation plan acceptable to USEPA and IEPA is uncertain.
audit_findings.explanation: The PRP exposure exists, but no remediation plan, allocation percentage or reasonably possible loss range is available. The latest filing reports no material development and targets remedy selection for December 2027 to February 2028. This is therefore a forward-looking contingent claim, not a presently measurable valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the feasibility study and remedy selection; obtain Watts's allocation, PRP funding capacity, insurance or indemnification coverage and existing accrual, then add a probability-weighted bridge deduction or cash-flow schedule when supportable.
